review.note: Draft by a non-clinician. Every vital value, rule threshold, timing and rubric item here is a fictional simulation parameter that has NOT been verified by a clinician. No dose appears anywhere on purpose. Do not activate for users before clinical review.

shared.persona: A man in his thirties, anxious, with a known bee-sting allergy and no other known medical problems. When short of breath he speaks in short sentences. What he knows and can say: he was stung on the arm a few minutes ago; hives spread over his chest and neck; his throat feels tight and his voice is hoarse; he has no known drug allergies and takes no regular medicines; he does not carry an auto-injector.

flags.airway_assessed: The trainee has assessed the airway: there is a hoarse voice, audible wheeze and a tight throat.
flags.help_called: Help / the emergency response has been called.
flags.trigger_removed: The trigger (the sting) has been dealt with.
flags.positioned: The patient has been positioned by the trainee.
flags.oxygen_on: The patient is receiving supplemental oxygen.
flags.fluids_given: An IV fluid bolus has been given.
flags.deteriorating: The patient is clearly getting worse.

actions.description: States, or clearly acts on, the recognition that this is anaphylaxis / a severe allergic reaction.
actions.outcome: The trainee has recognised a severe allergic reaction.

actions.description: Asks the patient questions about the event: what happened, trigger, allergies, medicines, past reactions.
actions.outcome: The patient answers the questions briefly, between breaths.

actions.description: Assesses airway and breathing: looks and listens, checks for swelling, hoarseness or wheeze, asks the patient to speak.
actions.outcome: The trainee checks the airway: the voice is hoarse, there is audible wheeze and the throat feels tight.

actions.description: Calls for help, activates the emergency response, or asks for the resuscitation team or an ambulance.
actions.outcome: Help has been called and is on the way.

actions.description: Removes the trigger: for example removes the stinger or moves the patient away from the allergen.
actions.outcome: The sting site has been dealt with.

actions.description: Attaches monitoring: pulse oximeter, blood pressure cuff or ECG.
actions.outcome: A monitor is attached and the readings are visible.

actions.description: Positions the patient appropriately: lying flat with legs raised, or sitting up if struggling to breathe.
actions.outcome: The patient has been positioned as ordered.

actions.description: Gives supplemental oxygen, for example by a high-flow mask.
actions.outcome: Oxygen is running through a mask.

actions.description: Gives epinephrine (adrenaline) by injection into the muscle, or orders it to be given.
actions.outcome: Epinephrine has been given; over the next minutes the patient starts to feel a little better.

actions.description: Gives an IV fluid bolus (for example saline) because of low blood pressure.
actions.blocked_note: There is no IV access yet, so fluids cannot be given.
actions.outcome: An IV fluid bolus is running.

actions.description: Gives an antihistamine or a steroid (second-line drugs).
actions.outcome: A second-line medicine is given. It does not reverse the emergency by itself.

actions.description: Plans observation after treatment for a possible delayed second reaction, or arranges admission.
actions.outcome: Observation after treatment has been planned.

actions.description: Reassures the patient or explains calmly what is happening and what will be done.
actions.outcome: The patient has been reassured and is a little calmer.

rules.narrate: The patient looks more distressed and the wheeze is louder.

rules.note: No epinephrine by turn 4: blood pressure falls (floor so it cannot run to zero).
rules.narrate: The patient is getting clearly worse: pale, sweaty and struggling to breathe.

rules.note: Oxygen saturation falls faster without oxygen.

rules.narrate: The patient is drowsy and answers only briefly.
The patient only groans and no longer speaks.
The patient has collapsed and does not respond.

rules.note: Recovery after epinephrine, without oxygen: slower.
Recovery after epinephrine, with oxygen: faster.

rules.narrate: The patient is more awake and talking again.
The patient is starting to respond to your voice.
The patient is beginning to stir and groan.

rules.note: Case complete: treated and observation planned.
rules.narrate: The patient is stable enough for the case to be handed over for observation.

en.title: Anaphylaxis, simulation [needs medical review]
en.system_prompt: SIMULATION, NEEDS MEDICAL REVIEW. A man in his thirties develops hives, throat tightness and wheeze minutes after a bee sting at a garden party, with falling blood pressure.
en.opening: You are called to a garden party. A man in his thirties was stung on the arm by a bee a few minutes ago. He is sitting on the grass, scratching hives that are spreading across his chest, and says his throat feels tight. He is anxious and breathing fast. What do you do first?
en.fallback_reply: The patient looks at you but cannot answer clearly right now.

rubric.AS-RECOGNISE: Recognises anaphylaxis (skin signs plus airway, breathing or circulation involvement after a likely trigger)
rubric.AS-AIRWAY: Assesses the airway and breathing early (voice, swelling, wheeze)
rubric.AS-EPI: Gives intramuscular epinephrine promptly, before second-line drugs such as antihistamines or steroids (dose and route per the locally approved protocol)
rubric.AS-HELP: Calls for help or the emergency response early and says clearly what is needed
rubric.AS-TRIGGER: Removes or stops further exposure to the trigger where possible
rubric.AS-POSITION: Positions the patient appropriately (flat with legs raised, or seated if struggling to breathe) and does not let them stand
rubric.AS-SUPPORT: Provides oxygen, establishes IV access and gives IV fluids for low blood pressure
rubric.AS-MONITOR: Attaches monitoring and rechecks the patient's response
rubric.AS-COMMS: Reassures the patient and gives clear, direct instructions to helpers
rubric.AS-OBSERVE: Plans observation for a delayed second reaction and considers repeating epinephrine if there is no response

ko.title: 아나필락시스 시뮬레이션 [의학 검토 필요]
ko.system_prompt: 시뮬레이션, 의학 검토 필요. 정원 파티에서 30대 남성이 벌에 쏘인 지 몇 분 만에 두드러기, 목 조임, 쌕쌕거림이 생기고 혈압이 떨어지고 있습니다.
ko.opening: 정원 파티 현장에 출동했습니다. 30대 남성이 몇 분 전 팔을 벌에 쏘였습니다. 그는 잔디에 앉아 가슴으로 번지는 두드러기를 긁으며 목이 조이는 느낌이 든다고 말합니다. 불안해하며 숨을 빠르게 쉬고 있습니다. 가장 먼저 무엇을 하시겠습니까?
ko.fallback_reply: 환자가 당신을 바라보지만 지금은 또렷하게 대답하지 못합니다.

rubric.AS-RECOGNISE: 아나필락시스(유발 요인 후 피부 증상과 기도·호흡·순환 이상)를 인지한다
rubric.AS-AIRWAY: 기도와 호흡(목소리, 부종, 쌕쌕거림)을 조기에 평가한다
rubric.AS-EPI: 항히스타민제나 스테로이드 같은 2차 약물보다 먼저 에피네프린을 신속히 근육주사한다(용량과 경로는 승인된 지역 프로토콜에 따름)
rubric.AS-HELP: 도움이나 응급 대응 체계를 조기에 요청하고 필요한 것을 명확히 말한다
rubric.AS-TRIGGER: 가능하면 유발 요인을 제거하거나 추가 노출을 막는다
rubric.AS-POSITION: 환자를 적절한 자세(다리를 올린 앙와위, 호흡곤란 시 앉은 자세)로 두고 일어서지 못하게 한다
rubric.AS-SUPPORT: 산소를 투여하고 정맥로를 확보하며 저혈압에는 수액을 투여한다
rubric.AS-MONITOR: 모니터링을 부착하고 환자의 반응을 다시 확인한다
rubric.AS-COMMS: 환자를 안심시키고 주변 인력에게 명확하고 직접적으로 지시한다
rubric.AS-OBSERVE: 지연된 2차 반응에 대비해 관찰을 계획하고 반응이 없으면 에피네프린 반복을 고려한다
